public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google and Anthropic have largely caught up with OpenAI, and Chinese companies are closing in.

statement.excerpt: Google and Anthropic have each largely caught up; various Chinese companies are closing in.

from_speaker: Google and Anthropic have each largely caught up
various Chinese companies are closing in
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading in this context concerns frontier model capabilities, not company revenue, market share, or profitability.
'Largely caught up' means broadly competitive performance across important capability evaluations; it does not require winning every task.
'Various Chinese companies' requires evidence concerning more than one Chinese developer.
'Closing in' requires improvement toward the frontier, rather than merely the existence of competing models.
The current comparison is assessed using evaluations public by February 13, 2026. The target period includes late 2025 because the statement also describes a recent direction of change.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations place Google and Anthropic alongside or ahead of OpenAI on important capabilities, while evaluations of at least two Chinese developers show meaningful progress toward that frontier.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show a persistent broad capability separation favoring OpenAI over Google or Anthropic, or show Chinese competitors collectively falling farther behind rather than approaching the frontier.

evidence.explanation: The original APEX-Agents evaluation places a Google model ahead of OpenAI on professional, multi-application tasks. This supports competitive capability in an important domain, although it is not a universal ranking.

The report places Opus 4.6 first on its ten-evaluation Intelligence Index, ahead of the previous leader GPT-5.2, and identifies leadership in agentic work, terminal coding, and physics. This supports Anthropic having caught up while preserving the report's task-specific qualifications.

The report describes Moonshot's model as closer to the frontier and places it behind only OpenAI and Anthropic on GDPval-AA. It also reports visual reasoning performance comparable to GPT-5.2 and Opus 4.5.
